Celebrity Golf Classic is a 3-day gathering of current and former professional athletes, actors, artists and business executives where we discuss our collective strategy to get the word out to men, women, our families, friends and our communities about the importance of âgetting checkedâ for prostate and colorectal cancer. The tragic passing of Chadwick Boseman, the talented actor, at the age of 43 came as a surprise and shock to many. For a seemingly healthy, relatively young man to die from colorectal cancer seems almost incomprehensible. Both prostate and colorectal cancer disproportionately affect the African American community, where the rates are the highest of any racial/ethnic group in the US. African Americans are about 20% more likely to get colorectal cancer and about 40% more likely to die from it than most other groups. And among African American men, 19 percent - nearly one in five â will be diagnosed and five percent of those will die from prostate cancer. In fact, colorectal cancer, is the second deadliest cancer in the country and prostate cancer is the fourth most common reason overall for death of African American men. Early-onset colorectal cancers have been increasing by about 2 percent per year since the mid-1990s. This increase has moved colorectal cancer up to being the top cause of cancer deaths in men under the age of 50 and the second-leading cause of cancer deaths in women under 50 in the United States. African Americans are disproportionately burdened by cancer in general. The reasons for these differences are complex, but they largely reflect differences in risk factors and in health care access, which historically, can also be related to socioeconomic status. They often experience greater obstacles to cancer prevention, detection, treatment, and survival, including systemic racial disparities that are complex and go beyond the obvious connection to cancer. The mission of the RL Gant Sports Get Checked! Celebrity Golf Classic is to get screening information in front of all attendees about this important health issue. Then you can take our collective messages back into locker rooms, onto film sets, backstage in dressing rooms, into business suites and into our homes. Carnaval Brasil Documentary Although Carnaval is celebrated in towns and villages throughout Brasil and other Catholic countries, Rio de Janeiro has long been regarded as the Carnaval Capital of the World. Carnaval Rio, is not only the biggest, it is also the benchmark against which every other Carnaval is compared. And one of the most interesting artistic events on the Globe. Occurring annually, with 5 days of celebration, 40 days before Easter. It usually happens in February, the hottest month in the Southern Hemisphere, when the Rio summer is at its peak. And almost everyone has heard of Carnaval Rio, and seen at least a glimpse of the TV coverage, which is watched with envy by millions around the world, all of them just wishing that they could be there. But no one has seen it the way Aladdin Artists will capture it. Aladdin Artists will delve deep into its origins and those responsible for continuing the tradition. We will talk with the composers of the music and take a deep look and close listen, to what makes the samba enredo, so compelling. And we will talk with one of the most involved groups in Carnaval Rio, the people of the favelas and feature their very important story. We will interview the residents and members of the local samba schools and see why they are deeply involved with the performance and costumes of their groups. We want to capture the pure essence of the samba schools who entertain the community through samba nights and create the pageantry for the Samba Parade. We will capture video of them picking the themes, writing the music and lyrics, making the costumes and floats and practicing all year to succeed in the SapucaÃ.
